feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible in ELM alone; fully feasible with PFLOTRAN. The core physics (vertical Richards-equation flow of an infiltration pulse through a variably-saturated column to the water table) requires a deep, finely-resolved unsaturated zone. Standard ELM uses a ~3.8 m, 10/15-layer hydrologic soil column that cannot represent a 50 m (or even 10-20 m) water table, so the deep cases must be run with ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling (or PFLOTRAN standalone) to solve Richards' equation over the full 0.5-50 m domain.
answerable: Fraction/timing of an infiltration pulse arriving at the water table as a function of initial WTD (0.5-50 m) using PFLOTRAN Richards solver
Shape/attenuation and travel-time (arrival lag) of the wetting-front pulse in the unsaturated zone
Water-table rise (recharge) response for shallow cases (<3.8 m) directly in ELM's soil hydrology
Sensitivity of pulse propagation to soil texture (retention/conductivity) at fixed WTD
not_answerable: Deep (>~4 m) water-table cases in default ELM without PFLOTRAN coupling
Lateral/3-D flow, capillary fringe dynamics beyond 1-D vertical resolution
Real-site absolute recharge (this is an idealized homogeneous-column experiment, not a calibrated field prediction)
Vapor-phase or preferential (macropore) transport unless explicitly parameterized

parsed.n_justification: One idealized column per initial water-table depth to sweep 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 m (roughly log-spaced). All columns share identical climate forcing, soil texture, and the same imposed infiltration pulse so that WTD is the only varied control, isolating its effect on pulse arrival fraction and timing.
requires_capabilities: ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling (or PFLOTRAN standalone) for variably-saturated Richards flow over deep (up to 50 m) columns
Custom vertical grid extending to >=50 m with fine (0.05-0.1 m) near-surface layering to resolve the wetting front
Prescribed/idealized infiltration pulse forcing (e.g., a single high-intensity precip event over a low-flux background)
Configurable bottom boundary condition (fixed head to set initial water-table depth) and hydrostatic initial condition
Homogeneous soil hydraulic property specification (Van Genuchten/Brooks-Corey) across the profile
assumptions: Idealized 1-D vertical homogeneous column; location (35N, 98W) chosen only to supply realistic reference climate, results are generic
Initial condition is hydrostatic equilibrium above a water table set at each target depth via a fixed-head lower boundary
A single, well-defined infiltration pulse (e.g., 50 mm over a few hours, followed by no rain) is applied so pulse tracking is unambiguous
Same soil texture (sandy loam) and same pulse magnitude across all 7 columns; only initial WTD differs
No lateral flow, no macropores, isothermal liquid-water transport (temperature output retained for diagnostics only)

'Fraction reaching water table' is diagnosed from cumulative QRECHARGE/QDRAI (ELM) or bottom-flux integration (PFLOTRAN) relative to applied pulse volume; 1-year run captures full drainage of the deepest case
